one_month_reasoning: Effective start $64.85 (after-hours 2026-10-20, -5.6% vs the $68.69 close, Twelve Data quote per the run brief). The main event in the window, Q3 results, has just printed: EPS $0.87 beat the $0.82 consensus and revenue $12.87B was in line, but the Q4 guide ($0.67 EPS vs $0.73 consensus, 26.0% margin incl. ~120bps layoff charge), the 2026 ad revenue cut (~$2.7B from ~$3B) and the FCF cut ($12.0B from $12.5B) are the second guide-down in a row. In the window: the regular session reaction and target cuts (Oct 21), the 10-Q (~Oct 22), the mid-November Nielsen Gauge (Netflix share of US TV ~7.8% in July). Expect mild negative drift after a guidance-driven miss and the break of the $65.08 52-week low, partly offset by a record $4.8B quarterly buyback pace. Median ~$64.3, spread ~11% (mix of 9.5% and 15% monthly vols; annual 37%/3.5 = 10.6%) with a fatter left tail.

fair_value.method: Engine set: 0.8 x P/E 18.0x on horizon NTM GAAP EPS ~$4.15 ($74.76) + 0.2 x driver DCF ($63.12; regional build to ~$70B revenue and 35% margin in 2030, WACC 9.5%, g 3%), less a probability-weighted acquisition-overpayment adjustment (-$2.25B); 4,062M horizon shares.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Horizon NTM GAAP EPS ~$4.15 (model; consensus ~$4.30) x 18.0x (NFLX now 18.2x NTM; core 8-peer median 22.4x, range 11.1x-35.4x)

inputs_detail.derivation: FY2026 regional revenue (FY2025 base x 2026 growth): UCAN 22,352, EMEA 16,547, LATAM 6,108, APAC 6,103 = $51.11B. FY2027 increments 22,352x8.5% = 1,900 + 16,547x10.5% = 1,737 + 6,108x11% = 672 + 6,103x13% = 793 = 5,102 -> +10.0%. Raised from 9.6% in round 1 because the CFO's stated objective on the Q3 call is to 'sustain double-digit revenue growth' (source 19), which I read as a floor management will manage to, not a guide; I keep it at the bottom of that range because ads are 'a bit behind our aggressive target' (19), the 2026 ad outlook was cut to ~$2.7B (1), engagement is soft (5, 6) and the next price-increase cycle is not guided. Ads ~$2.7B -> ~$3.7B (+37%) add ~2pts; subscription ~+8%.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Street implies ~11-12% (Q4 exit +12%); at +11.5% and the same margin FY2027 EPS would be ~2% higher and the horizon value ~+$2.5/share. Bear (ads stuck near $3.2B, churn after price rises) ~7%.

inputs_detail.derivation: 2026 = guided 31.5% (incl. ~30bps layoff charge). 2025 margin 29.5% (F10/F3). Then +1.5pts in 2027 (layoff savings ~1,000 roles, ad scale) slowing to +0.5pt/yr as sports/live costs and content inflation absorb operating leverage (Sarandos: live sports perform poorly on engagement vs cost). Below the 2027 32-37% street range midpoint.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Netflix's historic +2-3pts/yr margin expansion would put 2030 at ~38% and add ~$6/share via the P/E leg.

inputs_detail.derivation: Effective rate 2023 12.9% (797/6,205), 2024 12.6% (1,254/9,966), 2025 13.7% (1,741/12,723), TTM 17.2% (2,843/16,493, incl. fee income); 15% as a midpoint with a rising global minimum tax.
Q3'26 4,195 vs Q3'25 4,340 = -3.3%; ~$11B/yr buybacks at ~$70 retire ~157M (3.7%) less ~0.7% SBC/option issuance.

NFLX now $64.85 / NTM consensus EPS $3.62 (Q4'26 0.73 + Q1-Q3'27 0.93+0.98+0.98) = 17.9x (gate correction: written as $3.56 / 18.2x, which holds only with the $0.67 Q4 guide); on FY2027 $3.80 = 17.1x. I hold today's ~18x at the horizon (round 1 used 17x, which was a further de-rating I had not argued; corrected per supervisor). Core 8-peer median 22.4x (DIS 15.2, FOXA 11.1, WMG 18.5, META 22.2, GOOGL 340.27/14.97 = 22.7 on FY2027, AMZN 28.2, SPOT 526.08/17.28 = 30.4 on FY2027, TKO 35.4: median of 22.2 and 22.7). The ~20% discount persists because NFLX FY2028/FY2027 consensus EPS growth (+19%: 4.52/3.80) is below META (+23.5%), AMZN (+32.7%) and SPOT (+28%: 22.09/17.28) and measured engagement share is falling. The skeptic case is carried in below-consensus EPS (~$4.15 model vs ~$4.30 street NTM at the horizon) and the bear scenario, not in a lower multiple on top (that would count the same worry twice). Gate correction (2026-10-21, mixed basis): the 8-peer median mixed the run table's NTM fiscal-year blends with GOOGL and SPOT on calendar FY2027 alone. On one basis (peers.md NTM fiscal-year blend of Nasdaq.com/Zacks consensus EPS, Zacks basis for every name) the median is 20.4x: FOXA 11.1, DIS 15.2, WMG 18.5, META 22.2, AMZN 28.2, TKO 35.4 -> (18.5 + 22.2) / 2 = 20.35. GOOGL is dropped (its Zacks FY2026 EPS 20.55 includes non-operating stake gains); SPOT is out of the run table (EUR reporter) and on the same blend is 526.08 / (0.504 x 13.71 + 0.496 x 17.28 = 15.48) = 34.0x, which would make a 7-name median of 22.2x. The 18x multiple itself is unchanged (judgment).
inputs_detail.variant_view: 17x (further de-rating if the January FY2027 guide disappoints) costs ~$4.2 on the P/E leg (~$3.3 on fair value); the 22.4x median would add ~$18 on the leg; bear 14x gives ~$51 on the leg.

inputs_detail.value: ~$4.15 (engine: NOPAT less after-tax interest / horizon shares; P/E leg $74.76 / 18)
inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus NTM EPS at Oct-2027 ~ Q4'27 0.91 (3.80-0.93-0.98-0.98) + 0.75 x FY2028 4.52 = $4.30; my model is ~3.5% below on lower revenue growth (FY2028-30) and a margin path capped at 35%.

Netflix agreed an ~$83B deal for much of WBD in late 2025 and withdrew when Paramount raised (21); management showed willingness to do a large deal. With WBD gone to Paramount, fewer targets of that size remain, so I cut my round-1 probability from 20% to 15%; ~$15B of value destroyed (~18% of an $83B price, the typical acquirer overpayment I assume for a contested media deal) x 0.15.
inputs_detail.variant_view: No deal (most likely) adds back $0.55/share; a $50B+ deal at a 25% overpayment would cost ~$3/share in that state.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Regional revenue build 2026-2030 (+13.1%, +10.0%, ~+8.6%, ~+7.7%, ~+6.7%), EBIT margin 31.5%->35%, tax 15%, capex+content gap 5.5%->4.0%, WACC 9.5%, terminal g 3%, TV 83% of EV

inputs_detail.derivation: 10-K FY2025 total revenue.
10-K streaming revenue by region (thousands, rounded); sums to 45,183.0.

Calibrated to the Q3 letter full-year guide of $51.1B (+13%): H1 2026 revenue 24,810 vs 21,622 (+14.7%, from F6 derivation), Q3 regional growth UCAN 11%, EMEA 11%, LATAM 17%, APAC 12%, Q4 guide $13.4B (+12%); UCAN slower than the rest. Derived split (estimate), not guidance: the Q3 letter guides only the total ($51.1B, +13%). [gate 2026-10-21]
Fade toward a mature paid-streaming level: UCAN slowest (highest penetration, YouTube share of TV ~14% vs Netflix ~7.8%), APAC fastest (India view hours +24% in Q3).
inputs_detail.variant_view: If engagement stabilises and ads reach 10% of revenue, growth could hold ~2pts higher (bull deltas).

inputs_detail.derivation: Derived ratio (estimate): TTM D&A 372.4 / TTM revenue 48,370.8 = 0.77% (F39/F6); 6M 2026 199.1 / 24,809.7 = 0.80% (Q2 10-Q); FY2025 333.4 / 45,183.0 = 0.74%. 0.8% used (excludes content amortisation, which is inside EBIT). [gate 2026-10-21]

inputs_detail.input: Capex incl. content cash over amortisation
inputs_detail.derivation: Property capex TTM 818.8/48,370.8 = 1.7%. Content: 9M 2026 additions $14,934M vs amortisation $12,765M; guide ~1.1x cash/amortisation, ~10% of ~$17B amortisation = ~3.3% of revenue. 2026 raised for the Q4 real-estate deal (FCF guide cut $12.5B->$12.0B). Gap narrows as content growth slows.
inputs_detail.variant_view: At 1.0x cash/amortisation the gap disappears and FCF rises ~3% of revenue (DCF +~$8).

inputs_detail.derivation: Q3 letter: gross debt $15.3B, cash $8.2B, net debt $7.1B (non-GAAP). Leases excluded (EBIT is after rent; $2.9B lease obligations per 10-K).

Cost of equity 5.12% (10-year Treasury, 2026-10-20) + beta 0.94 x 5.0% ERP = 9.8%; beta 0.94 = Blume-adjusted 0.91 (2-year weekly NFLX vs SPY regression, Yahoo data, my calc: 0.67x0.91+0.33). Debt ~5.4% of capital ($15.3B gross debt vs ~$270B equity at $64.85) at ~5.2% pre-tax, 4.4% after 15% tax. Blend 0.946x9.8% + 0.054x4.4% = 9.5%.
inputs_detail.variant_view: At 8.8% (the WACC the multiple implies) the DCF would match the P/E leg (+$7 on the DCF leg).

inputs_detail.derivation: After 2030 growth of ~7%; nominal GDP-like 3% given attention-share risks (YouTube) and a maturing UCAN base.

bear.story: Engagement keeps sliding (US TV share below 7.5%, and fewer disclosed engagement data to disprove it), 2027 ads miss again (~$3.2B), price increases meet churn, and a closed Paramount-WBD (Paramount+ + HBO Max) bids up content and sports rights: revenue growth ~3pts lower every year, margin ~2.5pts lower, P/E de-rates to ~14x (DIS/WMG level), WACC +0.5pt.

base.story: Revenue growth decelerates from 13% (2026) to ~10% (2027, the bottom of management's 'sustain double-digit' objective) and ~7% by 2030; ads ~$2.7B -> ~$3.7B in 2027; margin +1.5pts in 2027 then +0.5pt/yr to 35% (sports/content inflation absorbs leverage); buybacks cut the share count ~3%/yr; the stock holds today's ~18x NTM GAAP EPS.

bull.story: Ads-led: the 15-country ad-tier expansion from March 2027 and ad-tech fixes put ads on WARC's path (Netflix ~9.2% of CTV ad spend in 2027, ~$4.5B) and toward Omdia's $8B by 2030; high-margin ad revenue adds ~2.5pts of growth and ~2pts of margin, engagement stabilises on the slate, P/E re-rates to ~21x (still below the 22.4x peer median).

comps_summary.peer_range: Core 8 peers NTM P/E 11.1x (FOXA) to 35.4x (TKO), median 22.4x (DIS 15.2, FOXA 11.1, WMG 18.5, META 22.2, GOOGL 22.7 on FY2027, AMZN 28.2, SPOT 30.4 on FY2027, TKO 35.4); CMCSA 6.3x, ROKU 45.5x, TTWO 34.1x, LYV 119.1x shown but excluded. EV/EBITDA NTM not in the peer table; trailing median 16.2x (DIS 9.8x, META 16.2x, AMZN 16.8x).
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 18.0x NTM GAAP P/E: ~20% below the 22.4x core median, equal to NFLX's own 18.2x NTM at $64.85. Round 1's 13.2x 'content subset' (incl. CMCSA) is dropped as a reference.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: A ~20% discount is argued to persist through the horizon: NFLX's FY2028/FY2027 consensus EPS growth (+19%) is below the ad-platform peers (META +23.5%, AMZN +32.7%, SPOT ~+28%), its measured engagement share is falling (US TV share 7.8% vs YouTube ~14%; hours/member ~8% below 2023) and it now discloses engagement only once a year, so the market has less evidence to re-rate it on. It holds a premium to DIS/FOXA/WMG on margin (31.5% vs low-teens to ~20%), a net-debt/EBIT below 0.5x and ~3%/yr buyback-driven share shrink. I take no further de-rating beyond today's multiple: the skeptic case is in the EPS path and the bear scenario.

thesis_break_reason: $50 is ~12x my horizon NTM EPS (~$4.15) and ~13x FY2027 consensus ($3.80), 23% below the $64.85 post-print price and just above my bear value ($48.7): trading there would mean the market is pricing falling earnings, not a multiple wobble: a January FY2027 guide below double-digit growth or with flat margins, churn after price increases, ads stuck near $3B after the 15-country launch, an expensive large acquisition, or a closed Paramount-WBD forcing a content/sports cost war. Unchanged from round 1 because my bear value moved only $2.5.

FY2027 margin: layoff savings vs sports/live and content cost inflation; street implies ~33%+

long_dated_risks.cash_flow_effect: One-off cash deposits and ~0.3pt of revenue in recurring levies

reverse_dcf_check: The 18x horizon P/E (P/E leg $74.76) equals the DCF at an ~8.5% WACC (engine reverse DCF) on my path: revenue growth 10.0% (2027) fading to ~6.7% (2030), EBIT margin to 35%, 3% terminal growth. At my 9.5% WACC the same multiple needs, by my rough sensitivity, about 1pt higher long-run growth or terminal margins in the high 30s. That is plausible only if ads scale toward Omdia's $8B and engagement stabilises; against probability-weighted long-dated risks of about -$7.7/share (attention share -4.2, sports/content inflation -1.4, Paramount-WBD -1.0, M&A -0.55, content commitments -0.3, levies -0.2) partly offset by +$0.75 from the ads upside (0.25 x $3), I hold today's 18x rather than the 22.4x median (which at 9.5% would need ~10% growth into the 2030s) and do not cut further.

sbc_treatment.note: GAAP EBIT and EPS after SBC (FY2025 SBC $368.4M, TTM $487.3M, ~1% of revenue); share count falls 3%/yr net of SBC issuance and buybacks, counted once. Peer P/Es are GAAP-based consensus (Zacks) where available.

reasoning: Skeptic lane, round 2. Supervisor findings acted on: (1) my 17x horizon P/E was a further de-rating below NFLX's own 18.2x NTM ($64.85/$3.56), not 'current level held'; I now hold ~18x and keep the skeptic view in below-consensus EPS (~$4.15 vs ~$4.30 street NTM at the horizon) and the bear case, so the worry is counted once. (2) Scenario weights 30/50/20 had no base rate and the downside news is in the $64.85 start: equalised to 25/50/25; asymmetry stays in severity (bear -4 turns, -3pt growth, -2.5pt margin). (3) Added an ads-led bull path (WARC 9.2% CTV share 2027, Omdia $8B by 2030: +2.5pt growth, +2pt margin, 21x). (4) Dropped the 13.2x content subset (it included cable); core 8-peer median 22.4x with SPOT added (526.08/17.28, my check at Nasdaq/Yahoo). (5) Added the Paramount-WBD long-dated risk I missed (12 states suing; $7B break fee if not closed by June 4, 2027). New evidence: the CFO's objective to 'sustain double-digit revenue growth' moved FY2027 growth 9.6% -> 10.0%; ads 'a bit behind our aggressive target'; Netflix moving to annual engagement reports (less disclosure, supports the discount); July target cuts (Pivotal $70 Street-low on short-form shift and content costs). WACC kept at 9.5% (Blume beta 0.94 on 2y weekly; supervisor's 9.4% with beta 1.0 differs by 0.1pt, under $0.5/share). FY2030 margin kept at 35% (supervisor 36%): live sports and a possible Paramount-WBD rights war argue for a lower cap. Engine: P/E $74.76 (0.8) + DCF $63.12 (0.2) - M&A adjustment -> $72.43; scenarios $48.7 / $72.4 / $94.3 at 25/50/25. Ladder: 50% scenario mixture (20% within-scenario vol) + 50% 37%-vol lognormal centred on the $64.85 start (today's price beats any blend as a 12-month forecast), with slightly fatter far-left tail; median ~$68.3, P(>=69) 0.49. 1-month ladder unchanged (no new in-window information). Option data not used; research limited to ~9 follow-up lookups; post-print analyst reactions not yet indexed.

bear.story: Engagement keeps sliding (US TV share below 7.5%, and fewer disclosed engagement data to disprove it), 2027 ads miss again (~$3.2B), price increases meet churn, and a closed Paramount-WBD (Paramount+ + HBO Max) bids up content and sports rights: revenue growth ~3pts lower every year, margin ~2.5pts lower, P/E de-rates to ~14x (DIS/WMG level), WACC +0.5pt.

base.story: Revenue growth decelerates from 13% (2026) to ~10% (2027, the bottom of management's 'sustain double-digit' objective) and ~7% by 2030; ads ~$2.7B -> ~$3.7B in 2027; margin +1.5pts in 2027 then +0.5pt/yr to 35% (sports/content inflation absorbs leverage); buybacks cut the share count ~3%/yr; the stock holds today's ~18x NTM GAAP EPS.

bull.story: Ads-led: the 15-country ad-tier expansion from March 2027 and ad-tech fixes put ads on WARC's path (Netflix ~9.2% of CTV ad spend in 2027, ~$4.5B) and toward Omdia's $8B by 2030; high-margin ad revenue adds ~2.5pts of growth and ~2pts of margin, engagement stabilises on the slate, P/E re-rates to ~21x (still below the 22.4x peer median).

model_inputs.structure_note: Streaming business with no reported segment margins: segment_build by the four reported regions (UCAN, EMEA, LATAM, APAC; revenue = paid memberships x ARM incl. ads; Netflix stopped reporting memberships in 2025, so growth is split into an implicit membership + price/ad path per region), uniform margins per year because only a company margin is guided. Content: EBIT is after content amortisation; the cash content spend in excess of amortisation (guided ~1.1x) is carried inside capex_pct_rev with property capex (~1.6% of revenue + ~3-4% content gap). Legs: P/E 18x on NTM GAAP EPS (0.80) and driver DCF (0.20, forward P/E 17.1x on FY2027 consensus $3.80 at $64.85 -> 15.0-19.6x band). No stakes, no SOTP: ads are not separable from subscription revenue in the filings. One equity adjustment: probability-weighted overpayment risk on another large acquisition (-$15B x 0.15).
model_inputs.gap_note: fair_value.value equals the engine's base horizon value for this set (72.43).
model_inputs.dcf_check: DCF $63.1 vs P/E leg $74.8 (-16%), inside the 20% band. The gap is the WACC: at 9.5% (10-year at 5.12%) the DCF sits below an 18x multiple, which implies ~8.5% (engine reverse DCF). Terminal value is 83% of DCF EV (3% Gordon growth after ~6.7% growth in 2030). I keep the DCF at its P/E-band weight 0.2 rather than lower the WACC: the gap is the skeptic's point that 18x already prices a lower discount rate than the risk-free rate supports.

inputs_detail.derivation: 10-K FY2025 total revenue.
10-K streaming revenue by region (thousands, rounded); sums to 45,183.0.

Calibrated to the Q3 letter full-year guide of $51.1B (+13%): H1 2026 revenue 24,810 vs 21,622 (+14.7%, from F6 derivation), Q3 regional growth UCAN 11%, EMEA 11%, LATAM 17%, APAC 12%, Q4 guide $13.4B (+12%); UCAN slower than the rest. Derived split (estimate), not guidance: the Q3 letter guides only the total ($51.1B, +13%). [gate 2026-10-21]

FY2026 regional revenue (FY2025 base x 2026 growth): UCAN 22,352, EMEA 16,547, LATAM 6,108, APAC 6,103 = $51.11B. FY2027 increments 22,352x8.5% = 1,900 + 16,547x10.5% = 1,737 + 6,108x11% = 672 + 6,103x13% = 793 = 5,102 -> +10.0%. Raised from 9.6% in round 1 because the CFO's stated objective on the Q3 call is to 'sustain double-digit revenue growth' (source 19), which I read as a floor management will manage to, not a guide; I keep it at the bottom of that range because ads are 'a bit behind our aggressive target' (19), the 2026 ad outlook was cut to ~$2.7B (1), engagement is soft (5, 6) and the next price-increase cycle is not guided. Ads ~$2.7B -> ~$3.7B (+37%) add ~2pts; subscription ~+8%.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Street implies ~11-12% (Q4 exit +12%); at +11.5% and the same margin FY2027 EPS would be ~2% higher and the horizon value ~+$2.5/share. Bear (ads stuck near $3.2B, churn after price rises) ~7%.

inputs_detail.derivation: Fade toward a mature paid-streaming level: UCAN slowest (highest penetration, YouTube share of TV ~14% vs Netflix ~7.8%), APAC fastest (India view hours +24% in Q3).
inputs_detail.variant_view: If engagement stabilises and ads reach 10% of revenue, growth could hold ~2pts higher (bull deltas).

inputs_detail.derivation: 2026 = guided 31.5% (incl. ~30bps layoff charge). 2025 margin 29.5% (F10/F3). Then +1.5pts in 2027 (layoff savings ~1,000 roles, ad scale) slowing to +0.5pt/yr as sports/live costs and content inflation absorb operating leverage (Sarandos: live sports perform poorly on engagement vs cost). Below the 2027 32-37% street range midpoint.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Netflix's historic +2-3pts/yr margin expansion would put 2030 at ~38% and add ~$6/share via the P/E leg.

inputs_detail.derivation: Effective rate 2023 12.9% (797/6,205), 2024 12.6% (1,254/9,966), 2025 13.7% (1,741/12,723), TTM 17.2% (2,843/16,493, incl. fee income); 15% as a midpoint with a rising global minimum tax.

Derived ratio (estimate): TTM D&A 372.4 / TTM revenue 48,370.8 = 0.77% (F39/F6); 6M 2026 199.1 / 24,809.7 = 0.80% (Q2 10-Q); FY2025 333.4 / 45,183.0 = 0.74%. 0.8% used (excludes content amortisation, which is inside EBIT). [gate 2026-10-21]

inputs_detail.input: Capex incl. content cash over amortisation
inputs_detail.derivation: Property capex TTM 818.8/48,370.8 = 1.7%. Content: 9M 2026 additions $14,934M vs amortisation $12,765M; guide ~1.1x cash/amortisation, ~10% of ~$17B amortisation = ~3.3% of revenue. 2026 raised for the Q4 real-estate deal (FCF guide cut $12.5B->$12.0B). Gap narrows as content growth slows.
inputs_detail.variant_view: At 1.0x cash/amortisation the gap disappears and FCF rises ~3% of revenue (DCF +~$8).

inputs_detail.derivation: My inference: Q1 2026 non-operating income (pretax H1 10,615.7 vs operating income H1 8,149.6, F88/F13 derivations) matches the ~$2.8B Warner Bros termination fee, so the ~$12.0B FCF guide includes it; ex-fee and after interest the underlying FCF is ~$9.5-10B, below my FCFF $11.3B, so the model's capex/content load is if anything light by ~$1B.
Q3 letter: gross debt $15.3B, cash $8.2B, net debt $7.1B (non-GAAP). Leases excluded (EBIT is after rent; $2.9B lease obligations per 10-K).
TTM interest expense 847.5 / total debt 14,309.3 = 5.9%; 5.5% on net debt.

inputs_detail.value: Q4 2026 at $12B annual rate; 20% of revenue from 2027 (~$11.2B)
inputs_detail.derivation: Q3 2026 buyback $4.8B (record), TTM $9.9B (F67), FY2025 $9.1B (F64), $22.3B authorisation left; 20% of revenue ~ 85% of model FCF.
Q3 letter diluted shares 4.195B (Q2: 4,261.3M, F33).
Q3'26 4,195 vs Q3'25 4,340 = -3.3%; ~$11B/yr buybacks at ~$70 retire ~157M (3.7%) less ~0.7% SBC/option issuance.

Cost of equity 5.12% (10-year Treasury, 2026-10-20) + beta 0.94 x 5.0% ERP = 9.8%; beta 0.94 = Blume-adjusted 0.91 (2-year weekly NFLX vs SPY regression, Yahoo data, my calc: 0.67x0.91+0.33). Debt ~5.4% of capital ($15.3B gross debt vs ~$270B equity at $64.85) at ~5.2% pre-tax, 4.4% after 15% tax. Blend 0.946x9.8% + 0.054x4.4% = 9.5%.
inputs_detail.variant_view: At 8.8% (the WACC the multiple implies) the DCF would match the P/E leg (+$7 on the DCF leg).

inputs_detail.derivation: After 2030 growth of ~7%; nominal GDP-like 3% given attention-share risks (YouTube) and a maturing UCAN base.

NFLX now $64.85 / NTM consensus EPS $3.62 (Q4'26 0.73 + Q1-Q3'27 0.93+0.98+0.98) = 17.9x (gate correction: written as $3.56 / 18.2x, which holds only with the $0.67 Q4 guide); on FY2027 $3.80 = 17.1x. I hold today's ~18x at the horizon (round 1 used 17x, which was a further de-rating I had not argued; corrected per supervisor). Core 8-peer median 22.4x (DIS 15.2, FOXA 11.1, WMG 18.5, META 22.2, GOOGL 340.27/14.97 = 22.7 on FY2027, AMZN 28.2, SPOT 526.08/17.28 = 30.4 on FY2027, TKO 35.4: median of 22.2 and 22.7). The ~20% discount persists because NFLX FY2028/FY2027 consensus EPS growth (+19%: 4.52/3.80) is below META (+23.5%), AMZN (+32.7%) and SPOT (+28%: 22.09/17.28) and measured engagement share is falling. The skeptic case is carried in below-consensus EPS (~$4.15 model vs ~$4.30 street NTM at the horizon) and the bear scenario, not in a lower multiple on top (that would count the same worry twice). Gate correction (2026-10-21, mixed basis): the 8-peer median mixed the run table's NTM fiscal-year blends with GOOGL and SPOT on calendar FY2027 alone. On one basis (peers.md NTM fiscal-year blend of Nasdaq.com/Zacks consensus EPS, Zacks basis for every name) the median is 20.4x: FOXA 11.1, DIS 15.2, WMG 18.5, META 22.2, AMZN 28.2, TKO 35.4 -> (18.5 + 22.2) / 2 = 20.35. GOOGL is dropped (its Zacks FY2026 EPS 20.55 includes non-operating stake gains); SPOT is out of the run table (EUR reporter) and on the same blend is 526.08 / (0.504 x 13.71 + 0.496 x 17.28 = 15.48) = 34.0x, which would make a 7-name median of 22.2x. The 18x multiple itself is unchanged (judgment).
inputs_detail.variant_view: 17x (further de-rating if the January FY2027 guide disappoints) costs ~$4.2 on the P/E leg (~$3.3 on fair value); the 22.4x median would add ~$18 on the leg; bear 14x gives ~$51 on the leg.

inputs_detail.value: ~$4.15 (engine: NOPAT less after-tax interest / horizon shares; P/E leg $74.76 / 18)
inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus NTM EPS at Oct-2027 ~ Q4'27 0.91 (3.80-0.93-0.98-0.98) + 0.75 x FY2028 4.52 = $4.30; my model is ~3.5% below on lower revenue growth (FY2028-30) and a margin path capped at 35%.
Netflix does not disclose regional operating margins; uniform margins make the build revenue-driven only.

Netflix agreed an ~$83B deal for much of WBD in late 2025 and withdrew when Paramount raised (21); management showed willingness to do a large deal. With WBD gone to Paramount, fewer targets of that size remain, so I cut my round-1 probability from 20% to 15%; ~$15B of value destroyed (~18% of an $83B price, the typical acquirer overpayment I assume for a contested media deal) x 0.15.
inputs_detail.variant_view: No deal (most likely) adds back $0.55/share; a $50B+ deal at a 25% overpayment would cost ~$3/share in that state.

inputs_detail.derivation: Round 1 used 0.30/0.50/0.20 with no base rate; the supervisor noted the downside news (ad cut, Q4 guide) is already in the $64.85 after-hours start. I equalise the tails: the bear deltas (-3pt growth, -2.5pt margin, -4 turns) and bull deltas (+2.5pt, +2pt, +3 turns) are already asymmetric in size (bear -$23.7 vs bull +$21.9 from base), so the skeptic tilt sits in severity, not probability.

inputs_detail.value: ads ~$4.5B in 2027, toward $8B by 2030 -> growth +2.5pt, margin +2pt, P/E 21x
inputs_detail.derivation: WARC: Netflix 3.7% of CTV ad spend in 2025 -> 9.2% in 2027, a 2.49x share gain; on 2025 ad revenue of >$1.5B (Omdia, 20) that is >$3.7B in 2027 before any growth in the CTV market itself; Omdia sees $8B by 2030 (20). Bull: ads repeat most of 2026's pace ('growing over 80% this year', 19): ~$2.7B (1) x 1.67 = ~$4.5B in 2027, which needs the WARC share path plus ~10%/yr CTV market growth (my judgment). That is ~$0.8B above my base $3.7B (~+1.6pt of 2027 growth on $51.1B); with the 15 new ad countries from March 2027 and the path to $8B, I use +2.5pt a year through 2030. Incremental ad revenue at high margin lifts EBIT margin ~2pt.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Management itself is 'a bit behind our aggressive target' (19); ads at $3.2B (bear) take ~1pt off 2027 growth.
